rules.title: `ecrecover` without a zero-address or identity check
rules.rationale: `ecrecover` returns `address(0)` when the signature is malformed. Using that value as a signer, or skipping a match against a known address, lets a bad signature pass as a valid one.

rules.title: Ether `transfer`/`send` (2300-gas stipend) used instead of `call`
rules.rationale: `address.transfer` and `address.send` forward only 2300 gas. A recipient that does more than log an event will fail, and the stipend is too small after gas-cost changes. Send value with `call` and check the success flag.

rules.title: Floating Solidity pragma (`^`, `~`, `>=`) in a deployable source
rules.rationale: A floating pragma lets every build pick a different compiler, so the bytecode you tested and audited may not be the bytecode you deploy. Pin one exact version in contracts and libraries. Tests, scripts, mocks and interface-only files are skipped.

rules.title: `abi.encodePacked` of dynamic types can collide
rules.rationale: `abi.encodePacked` concatenates values without a length prefix. Two dynamic values such as `string` or `bytes` can be split in more than one way and still hash to the same digest, so signatures, merkle leaves, and uniqueness checks built on that hash can be forged. Use `abi.encode`, which length-prefixes each value.

rules.title: Upgradeable initializer left public, or `_disableInitializers` missing
rules.rationale: A public `initialize` without the `initializer` lock can be called more than once and taken over. An implementation that never calls `_disableInitializers` in its constructor can also be initialized directly, which lets an attacker own the implementation and, on UUPS proxies, the proxy behind it. Lock the initializer and disable it in the constructor.

rules.title: Signature replay: signed data has no nonce, deadline, or chain id
rules.rationale: A signature stays valid for as long as the data it covers stays valid. If that data has no nonce the same signature can be submitted again, with no deadline it never expires, and with no chain id it can be replayed on a fork or another chain where the contract is deployed. Hash a per-signer nonce, a deadline, and `block.chainid` (or an EIP-712 domain separator) into the signed digest, and consume the nonce when the signature is used.

rules.title: `extcodesize == 0` used as an EOA check
rules.rationale: A zero code size does not mean the caller is an EOA. During construction a contract has no code yet, so `extcodesize` and `address.code.length` are zero and the check lets it in. EIP-7702 delegated accounts are EOAs that do have code, so the same check also rejects real users. Do not gate privileged actions on code size; authenticate the caller instead.
